s0.p86: Every time a new dependency is installed, npm automatically updates the lock file named **_⟦f29⟧_**
s0.p87: **_⟦f29⟧_** is a ‘snapshot’ of the current dependency tree, which accurately describes the folder structure in the ⟦f19⟧ directory

s0.p89: **_⟦f29⟧_** includes an **_integrity_** field to verify the package’s integrity
s0.p90: ^^Specifying a particular package version in **_⟦f1⟧_** fixes only top-level dependencies^^
s0.p91: ^^If your application is run on another machine (the user’s), different versions of lower-level packages may be installed, which could cause the application to malfunction^^
s0.p92: ^^To ensure that the end user of your application always sees a dependency tree identical to yours at the time of publication, you should use **_⟦f30⟧_** to create an exact snapshot of these dependencies and publish this snapshot alongside the application^^
s0.p93: Every time the application is deployed ( _deploy_ ), Node.js runs **_npm_**
s0.p94: ^^Deployment may be significantly delayed due to the installation of new versions of the packages listed in your application’s dependencies^^
s0.p95: ^^You can avoid updating dependencies by creating a **_npm-shrinkwrap.json_** file, which locks in the current versions of your application’s dependencies^^
s0.p96: ^^The format of this file is identical to that of **_⟦f29⟧_**^^
